title: the ticket inspector checks an outcomes plan's claims as it checks falsifier clauses
intention: The ticket inspector judges an outcomes plan: every outcome with a claim is checked as a clause is today, and an outcome with no claim is named as awaiting judgement, never as malformed.
why: Measured 2026-11-14: Q#100 is answered and the plan becomes outcomes (outline 9.3.5.1.2.1); this component reads ticket plans, so by RULE 1 its dual-read is its own ticket, a sibling of aa3e9a70db47 (the migration).
traces_to: Law 5 (the plan carries what a builder needs now), RULE 1 (each reader changes inside its own component); outline 9.3.5.1.2.1.
how: Dual-read during the change: compose base's published plan view (5c1e0a7d93b2); after: 5c1e0a7d93b2.

clauses.claim: an outcomes ticket is judged clause by clause over its claims, and a no-claim outcome is named awaiting judgement
a falsifier-clauses ticket and a prose-falsifier ticket get the findings they get on main

decisions.text: D1: inspector.py's falsifier check (~line 95-163) runs over plan.clauses(t) when the plan carries outcomes, and names each n in plan.awaiting(t) as awaiting judgement. It composes cairn.tools.base.plan (ticket 5c1e0a7d93b2): clauses(doc) gives [{n, claim}] from outcomes that carry a claim, else falsifier.clauses; steps(doc) gives [{n, text, writes_to, reads, after}] from outcomes (text = claim, else the migrated text), else decisions; it keeps no second reading of either shape.

D2: the red-first proof feeds the reader one ticket in each shape carrying the same content, one tooth per clause. test_inspector.py's test_roster_coverage gains one fixture firing outcome_awaiting_judgement (an outcome with no claim), since it requires a fixture for every ROSTER check.

measured.saw: Akien answered Q#100 (open-7aee6f89e4d9, open-82f27105184f): "rather than tasks should we be focused on outcomes?" ... "yes, we're in agreement. signed -amm". Outline 9.3.5.1.2.1: a plan is constraints, then outcomes {n, claim, writes_to, reads, after, via?}, then resources; the falsifier's clauses merge into the outcomes (old clause n stays outcome n); during the change every reader accepts both shapes, one sibling ticket per reader component.
measured.how: his answer, relayed verbatim by orchestrator; recorded at the question door; outline 9.3.5.1.2.1

measured.saw: test_inspector.py::test_roster_coverage requires a fixture firing every ROSTER check, so the new outcome_awaiting_judgement check needs one (+3 lines); 30/30 against the change and against main
